sections.h2: Fastest ways to sell in Amarillo
sections.html:
A house in good shape can go through an agent if you can wait for a buyer with a loan. When speed, repairs or a tenant complicate a regular listing, a cash sale is the alternative. Amarillo is the commercial hub of the Texas Panhandle, with an estimated 205,130 residents in mid-2025.

Amarillo spreads over two counties, so first find out which one holds your parcel. Most of the city is in Potter County, while a portion extends into Randall County. The tax office, clerk and appraisal records you need follow from that.

  • Look up the address with the Potter Randall Appraisal District, which covers ownership for both counties.
  • Call the tax office printed on your tax statement early.
  • Ask the City of Amarillo's Building Safety office about open permits on the property.

Amarillo is one of the more affordable Texas cities. Typical home values sit under $200,000, and about four in ten households rent. The 2020 count was 200,393 people, up from 190,695 in 2010.

sections.h2: Taxes on the Randall County side
sections.html:
Randall County sends statements on October 1 and treats them as payable immediately. Penalty and interest start only if the bill is unpaid after January 31, so February 1 is the first delinquent day. A check sent by first-class mail is treated as paid on its postmark date.

The county tax office also explains what a sale does to the bill:

  • The taxing unit never divides the year between buyer and seller. Most sales contracts do, which makes the contract and closing statement the documents to read.
  • The person who held title on the first of January of the prior year remains responsible for that year's tax, although the lien lets the unit pursue the buyer as well.
  • Four installments are open to homesteads of owners over 65, disabled owners and disabled vets. The first fourth and a signed agreement are due by January 31, and a first payment received by February 28 carries 7% penalty and interest. Skip a later installment and 6% penalty plus 1% interest accrue monthly.

On a tax certificate you will find delinquent taxes, penalties and interest, broken out by taxing unit. The fee is $10 in certified funds when you pick it up. Email your request and collect it in Canyon or Amarillo. To get a zero-balance certificate when taxes are due, pay with cash or certified funds, or wait 10 working days for a check to clear.

The Potter Randall Appraisal District is at 5701 Hollywood Road, Amarillo, phone 806-358-1601, mailing address P.O. Box 7190, Amarillo, TX 79114. For a parcel in Potter County, ask the Potter County tax assessor-collector for the same certificate.

sections.h2: Permits and the certificate of occupancy
sections.html:
The Building Safety office sits in the Simms Municipal Building, 808 S Buchanan Street, Suite 104, and keeps weekday hours of eight to five. You file permits online through MGO Connect. City ordinance Sec. 4-10-21 bars use of land until a Certificate of Occupancy and Compliance has been issued.

A new building receives its certificate as soon as the permit is completed. Anything else needs a separate one: a change of use, or a property that never got one. Alterations require a remodel or repair permit, and a registered contractor has to pull it. If the house has a converted garage, a rented room or a home business, ask Building Safety whether the certificate still matches how the property is used.

Splitting off part of a lot for sale triggers a platting requirement. Any tract inside the city limits needs a plat, and so does a tract of five acres or less in the extraterritorial jurisdiction that stretches five miles past the limits.

sections.h2: Does flood risk affect an Amarillo sale?
sections.html:
It can. Flooding in 1888 and 1889 pushed the original town to higher ground, and drainage on the High Plains remains a regular question from buyers. Randall County defines a 100-year flood as one with a 1% or greater chance of being equaled or exceeded in any year, which is different from a flood that comes once a century.

  • The county floodplain administrator will give you flood information if you provide the Randall appraisal ID, the address and the legal description.
  • On the Flood Insurance Rate Map, special flood hazard areas are shaded in. A Letter of Map Amendment takes out a property that was mapped in by mistake.
  • Work or repairs costing 50% or more of a building's market value count as substantial improvement or substantial damage under county rules.
  • Skipping a required county floodplain permit can mean fines up to $500 per day.

Whatever the map says, a buyer's lender may still insist on flood insurance.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or rented?
sections.html:
A few Texas deadlines apply here, and they are the same ones used across the state.

  • Inherited: an heir missing from the recorded deed can still claim the homestead exemption by handing the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.
  • Behind on payments: a lender typically holds off until the loan is over 120 days late, then must mail the sale notice 21 or more days before the first-Tuesday auction.
  • Tenants: the lease can set its own notice period, and otherwise the written notice to vacate is three days or more. A justice court hears the eviction case, and the writ of possession can issue six days after judgment.

Each of these can end in a sale, and an early decision leaves more room to negotiate.

sections.h2: What happens between contract and closing
sections.html:
Once a buyer signs, the title company orders a tax certificate from the Randall or Potter County office, gathers payoff letters and looks for open permits on the parcel. You then sign the deed before a notary, and the deed travels to the clerk in the county that holds the parcel.

Expect some back and forth over the tax figure, since the certificate has to cover every taxing unit. If the house is held through an estate, bring papers that show who has authority to sign.

sections.h2: Cash sale or agent listing in Amarillo
sections.html:
Begin with a list of what you owe: the mortgage payoff, any unpaid tax and the repairs a buyer is likely to demand. Set that beside what a listing might bring after weeks of showings and a lender's approval of the buyer. Cash offers tend to come in lower, yet they erase the repair list, the haggling after inspection and the chance that a loan collapses.

Before you agree to either, order a tax certificate so no unpaid year appears at closing, confirm which county records the deed, and ask Building Safety if the certificate of occupancy fits the house as it is today. Those three answers let you sign with confidence and choose a closing date that suits you. If a mortgage is involved, ask the lender for a written payoff figure at the same time.

faqs.q: Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?
faqs.a: Both. Most of the city is in Potter County and the rest reaches into Randall County, so your parcel decides which one applies.

faqs.q: When are Randall County property taxes due?
faqs.a: On receipt. Pay by January 31 to avoid penalty and interest. Statements are mailed each October 1, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1.

faqs.q: How much is a tax certificate in Randall County?
faqs.a: The fee is $10 in certified funds, collected when you pick it up in Canyon or Amarillo. It shows any delinquent taxes unit by unit.

faqs.q: Does Amarillo require a Certificate of Occupancy?
faqs.a: Yes, city ordinance Sec. 4-10-21 requires it. New buildings get one automatically, while an older property may need one if none was ever issued or its use has changed.

faqs.q: What does an Amarillo owner-occupied home typically cost?
faqs.a: The middle value for owner-occupied homes in Amarillo is $196,900 in the 2020-2024 estimates.
